In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the α1K276 startle disease mutation causes the channel to be less sensitive to glycine, and to open with less frequency and for shorter periods of time, than the wild-type channel.
the K276E disease mutation causes a loss of channel function by reducing the receptor’s ability to reach the fully liganded state and that this is due to a slowing of the channel gating process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the α1K276 mutation causes hyperekplexia by reducing the number of open channels and slowing their gating.
the K276E startle disease mutation causes hyperekplexia by slowing channel gating and by reducing the number of open states.
the K276E mutant is a useful tool to investigate the activation mechanism of glycine receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the K276E glycine receptor mutation, which is associated with startle disease, slows channel gating and reveals multiple closed states in the activation pathway.
the K276E mutant glycine receptor provides a new example of an ion channel in which the activation pathway contains more than one fully open state.
glycine receptor gating can be described by models that contain more than one fully bound open state.
